files.lesson.md: --- order: 30 unit: solids9 node: AC9M9M01 n3 uses: [AC9M9M01 n1, AC9M9M01 n2] assumes: [AC9M9M01 n2] connection: can-design title: Area and volume problems summary: "Real problems use both: the volume says how much it holds and the surface area says how much material it needs. Choose the right measure, then check the units." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A can has to hold 375 mL. What shape uses the least metal, and why don't real cans look like that?" --- A drinks company wants a can that holds 375 mL using as little metal as possible. A can's volume is fixed, but its shape isn't: it can be tall and thin or short and wide. Have a guess which uses least metal, and we'll come back to it at the end. (1 mL is 1 cm³.) ## Predict: which shape ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing the can that uses least metal shows whether students think the tallest, the shortest or something in between wins." check: type: predict q: "Three cans all hold 375 mL: one tall and thin, one medium, one short and wide. Which uses the least metal?" options: - "The medium one" - "The tall and thin one" - "The short and wide one" - "They all use the same" actual: "The medium one, with the height about the same as the width across the can. Tall and thin cans waste metal on the curved side, and short and wide ones on the ends." ``` ## Run: try a few radii ```step stage: run insight: "For a fixed volume, the height follows from the radius: h = V ÷ (πr²). Then the surface area follows." check: { type: number, q: "A can holds $375$ cm³ and has radius $4$ cm. What is its height? ($\\pi \\approx 3.14$; 1 decimal place)", answer: 7.5, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "375 ÷ (3.14 × 16) = 375 ÷ 50.24 = 7.46, about 7.5 cm." } ``` ## Investigate: compare surface areas ```step stage: investigate insight: "Surface area is in square units and volume is in cubic units: always check the units match the question." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A can of radius 4 cm and height 7.5 cm has total surface area $2\\pi r^2 + 2\\pi r h$. What is it? (cm², nearest whole number, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)" answer: 289 tolerance: 3 explain: "2 × 3.14 × 16 + 2 × 3.14 × 4 × 7.5 = 100.5 + 188.4 = 288.9, about 289 cm²." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $2 \\times 3.14 \\times 16$? (1 decimal place)", answer: 100.5, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "2 × 3.14 × 16 = 100.48." } - check: type: question q: "A can with radius 3 cm and height 13.3 cm has surface area 306 cm². A can with radius 4 cm and height 7.5 cm has 289 cm². Both hold 375 mL. Which uses less metal?" options: ["The radius 4 cm can", "The radius 3 cm can", "They use the same", "Can't tell"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "306 is more than 289.", "The surface areas differ.", "Compare the numbers."] explain: "Less surface area means less metal: 289 < 306." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#bea" text: "Bea compares two cans. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: units-area-volume-mixed explain: "Line 3: surface area is in cm², not cm³. Cubic units are for volume." ``` ### Same volume, different shapes ```worked V = \pi r^2 h = 375 :: The volume is fixed. h = 375 \div (\pi r^2) :: Height from the radius. r = 3 \Rightarrow h = 13.3, \; SA = 306 :: A tall can. r = 4 \Rightarrow h = 7.5, \; SA = 289 :: A medium can. r = 5 \Rightarrow h = 4.8, \; SA = 307 :: A wide can. \text{least metal near } r \approx 3.9, \; h \approx 7.8 :: Height about the width. ``` ### Which can ### Find the mistake Read Bea's working. Which line has the wrong units? ## Modify: change the target ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the size of the can, or the question, tests choosing surface area or volume for the job." tasks: - hint: ["It is a covering question.", "Surface area."] check: { type: question, q: "You want to know how much paint covers a box. Do you need its volume or its surface area?", options: ["Surface area", "Volume", "Both", "Neither"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Paint covers the outside, which is an area.", "Only the outside is painted.", "Paint covers a surface."], explain: "Painting covers the outside: surface area, in square units." } - hint: ["It is a filling question.", "Volume."] check: { type: question, q: "You want to know how much a can holds. Volume or surface area?", options: ["Volume", "Surface area", "Both", "Neither"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Holding means the space inside.", "Only the inside space counts.", "Holding is about the space inside."], explain: "How much it holds is the volume, in cubic units." } - hint: ["Real cans must be stacked, held and printed.", "Height about the width is best for metal; real cans are often taller."] check: { type: question, q: "The least-metal can has its height about equal to its width. Real drink cans are taller. Why might that be?", options: ["Taller cans are easier to hold and stack, so metal isn't the only thing that matters", "The calculation is wrong", "Taller cans use less metal", "Real cans are the same shape"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "The calculation is fine: the design has other goals.", "That is the opposite of what the table shows.", "They are taller than the minimum."], explain: "A model for one goal (least metal) ignores others: grip, stacking, labels and cost." } ``` ### Paint a box ### Fill a can ### Why real cans differ ## Practise: choose the measure ```step stage: practise insight: "Choosing volume or surface area and giving the right units." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A box is 3 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm. What is its volume? (cm³)" answer: 60 explain: "3 × 4 × 5 = 60." - check: type: number q: "What is the total surface area of that box? (cm²)" answer: 94 explain: "2 × (12 + 15 + 20) = 94." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $3 \\times 4 + 3 \\times 5 + 4 \\times 5$?", answer: 47, explain: "12 + 15 + 20 = 47." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a cylinder has radius 2 cm and height 5 cm. What is its volume? (cm³, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)" answer: 62.8 tolerance: 0.2 explain: "3.14 × 4 × 5 = 62.8." ``` ### Volume ### Surface area ### Review ## Make: design the can ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the can: use the table to pick a radius and say what the design gives up." tasks: - hint: ["Compare the surface areas from the table.", "Smaller area means less metal."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Compare cans holding 375 cm³ with radius 3 cm (surface area 306 cm²), 4 cm (289 cm²) and 5 cm (307 cm²). Which radius uses the least metal, and how much less than the radius 5 cm can? (cm²)" steps: - ["$306, 289, 307$", "the three surface areas"] - ["least is $289$ at radius 4 cm", "smallest of the three"] - ["$307 - 289 = 18$", "the saving over radius 5"] answer: "18" answerLabel: "Metal saved (cm²)" tolerance: 0.5 feedback: - ["289", "That's the least area. Find how much less than the radius 5 cm can."] - ["4", "That's the radius. Find the saving."] criteria: - "I compared all three areas." - "I took the difference." - "I gave the unit." explain: "307 − 289 = 18 cm² saved." - check: type: question q: "Why is a table of three radii not enough to be sure which is best?" options: ["The best radius could be between the ones tried", "Tables are always wrong", "Only one radius is allowed", "Surface area doesn't matter"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A table is a fair start.", "Any radius could be used.", "It's the goal of the problem."] explain: "The true best is near r = 3.9, between 3 and 4. A finer table would show it." ``` ### The best radius ### Is three enough The can sizes are calculated for the task (π ≈ 3.14, 1 mL = 1 cm³). **Also used in** - **Packaging.** Less material means lower cost and less waste. - **Engineering.** Pressure vessels and tanks balance material against capacity. - **Next unit.** Measurement error: every measurement is an estimate. ```teacher summary: Students choose between surface area and volume, and use both to compare designs (AC9M9M01, node 3). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can choose surface area or volume for the question. - I can give the right units. - I can compare designs with a table. struggle: "Mixing up area and volume. Ask: is it a covering question or a filling question?" before: > Students need Volume of prisms and cylinders. The one idea: covering is area, filling is volume. A table of cases is how to compare. The best can has height about equal to its width (diameter = height at the minimum). Values are calculated with π ≈ 3.14. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the can design in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student writes cm³ for a surface area. ask: Is it a flat covering or a space inside? fix: Area is cm², volume is cm³. stretch: Use a spreadsheet to find the radius that gives the least metal. support: A printed table with the radius and height filled in. leads: | Continues AC9M9M01 node 3. Where it leads: Measurement error. exit: q: "Paint covering a wall: area or volume?" a: Area. explain: > Covering needs surface area (square units). Filling needs volume (cubic units). A table of designs for the same volume shows which uses least material. ```

# region: bea
Can A: radius 3 cm, height 13.3 cm. Can B: radius 4 cm, height 7.5 cm.

So can B uses 17 cm³ less metal.
